title: A Study Of Sleep Restriction On Glycemic Control And Cardiovascular Risk Mechanisms In Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
official: Effects Of Sleep Restriction On Glycemic Control And Cardiovascular Risk Mechanisms In Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
summary: The purpose of this research is to learn whether lack of sleep in people with type 1 diabetes affects blood sugar control, and whether it leads to changes in heart and blood vessel function or memory and thinking ability.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Male or female between age of 18-60 yrs.
* T1D diagnosis will be confirmed if needed by C- Peptide (≤0.3 ng/ml) with a simultaneous fasting glucose concentration 80-225 mg/ dL.
* T1D without known atherosclerotic vascular disease
* HbA1c ≤7.5%
* Average sleep duration 7 to 9 hours per night
* Willing to complete study procedures
* An understanding of and willingness to follow the protocol and sign the informed consent.
* Non-smoker

Exclusion Criteria:

* Anti-hyperglycemic drugs other than insulin and metformin.
* Pregnancy or contemplating pregnancy in study
* BMI ≥35 kg/m2
* Obstructive sleep apnea
* Unidentified sleep abnormalities - sleep test and sleep history will be done in each subject before proceeding with the study; any significant sleep abnormality found will be an exclusion criterion.
* Uncontrolled hypertension; resting blood pressure ≥ 140/90 mmHg and/or ≥ 2 antihypertensive medications
* Clinically diagnosed obstructive coronary artery disease or heart failure
* Abnormal sleep and eating patterns.
* Vulnerable individuals including prisoners will not be enrolled for these studies.
* Uncontrolled or recurrent ventricular tachycardia
* Previous organ transplant with or without current graft function
* Currently receiving chemotherapy or long-term immunosuppressant (steroids etc) therapy
* Clinically diagnosed Autonomic Neuropathy
* Recent history of abnormal liver function test results (Transaminase \>3 times the upper limit of normal)
* Recent history of abnormal renal function test results (calculated GFR \<60 mL/min/1.73m2)
* Active gastroparesis
* Abuse of alcohol or recreational drugs
* Infectious process not anticipated to resolve prior to study procedures (e.g. meningitis, pneumonia, osteomyelitis).
* If on anti-depressant, lack of stability on the medication for the past 2 months prior to enrollment in the study
* Any known medical condition that in the judgment of the investigator might interfere with the completion of the protocol such as the following examples:
* Inpatient psychiatric treatment in the past 6 months
* Presence of a known adrenal disorder
* A recent injury to body or limb, muscular disorder, use of any medication, any carcinogenic disease, or other significant medical disorder if that injury, medication or disease in the judgment of the investigator will affect the completion of the protocol.
* Chronic diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma
* Participating in any other treatment study
